current.text: He came back early from a torn Achilles last season. He finished 19th per game in limited minutes and played 35 minutes a night in the playoffs. He said he played at about 80 to 85%.
He missed playoff Game 7 with knee inflammation from compensating for the Achilles. The knee issue is not chronic and needed no surgery.
Experts are not worried about the Achilles. The Game 7 knee problem is their only health concern, and one expert rates that risk at about 1%. He is expected to arrive fully healthy.
After the Achilles injury, his rim finishing fell from 69% to 60%.
His FG% should go up, and he should return to his best level.
He is expected to play back-to-backs, including the three Boston has in our playoff window.
Jaylen Brown is gone from Boston, and Paul George has joined the team.
Tatum is the first option, with George clearly second. Experts expect a big usage season, with more usage than last season.
Boston has 16 back-to-backs, tied for the most in the league.
Boston plays 4, 3 and 4 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. That is one game short of the maximum, and the window includes three back-to-backs.
Boston is projected to win about 48 games and to be better than last season.

Experts are comfortable taking him in round one, around picks 6 to 8, and call his rank of 7 to 8 about right. One says an ESPN ADP of 12 is too late. The newest view, from early October, is neutral: he is one of many first-round players bunched together.
He went for 46 USD in an expert auction mock draft on 2026-10-05.
Josh would pay more than 45 USD for him. He held off only because he did not want to spend over 40 USD on any one player.

durable.text: His threes and points are league outliers. His rebounds and assists are strong for a forward. His turnovers are high for a forward.
Lloyd names blocks, steals and FG% as his weak categories.
He was seen as an iron man before he tore his Achilles. Knee inflammation from compensating for the Achilles followed.

note: Both sites rank him 7th, at 54 USD on Yahoo and 58 USD on ESPN, but he went for only 46 USD in an expert auction mock. Around 50 USD is a fair price for a first-round forward who brings elite threes and points with strong rebounds and assists. He fits punt TO builds best, and his FG% is the soft spot. Early in the season, check that the knee is fine, that his FG% and rim finishing recover from last season's 41.1%, and that he plays Boston's many back-to-backs.
